Everything in this section is a placeholder until you fill it.?? # BRC and AI tools {#how-the-brc-uses-ai background-color="#23373B" .center .middle} ## How the BRC uses AI ??How the BRC uses AI in its own work: where it helps and where we don't use it. Ties back to the strengths and limitations section, with one or two concrete examples from past projects (e.g. the SCENIC+ example).?? ## What we have learned ??Lessons from using AI on core facility projects: what went well, what cost more time than it saved, and what we changed as a result.?? # Tools and resources from the BRC {#tools-and-resources-from-the-brc background-color="#23373B" .center .middle} ## BRC tools available through RU Claude Rockefeller intends to make RU-developed methods, for example BRC's tools, available via RU Claude (see *AI Strategy at Rockefeller*). ??List the BRC tools and resources that will be available this way, how to access them and their current status (available now / planned).?? ## The BRC plugin for Claude Ask questions of your sequencing data **in plain English**. Claude finds the samples, runs BRC pipelines and writes the report. ```{mermaid} flowchart LR U(["You
'Compare EpSC vs SB
and flag bad samples'"]) --> C["Claude +
BRC plugin"] C --> S["Skills
BRC workflows
and known pitfalls"] C --> M["Connector (MCP)
secure, scoped
to your lab"] M --> D[("BRC data and compute
pipeline samples · QC
DESeq2 on the HPC
lab expression matrices
single-cell datasets
IGV · BRC training")] ``` ::::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"} ::: notes The plugin bundles two things from the Customizing session: skills (how the BRC runs a DE analysis, which QC numbers matter, common traps such as reused sample names) and an MCP connector to the BRC server. The connector only exposes defined tools: Claude can't browse the server freely. Access follows your lab login. ::: ::::: ## What you can do with it {.smaller} :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} **Bulk RNA-seq** - Find your lab's samples and sequencing runs - **QC** every library and flag failed ones - Run a **differential expression** report on the HPC (previewed first, run only with your OK) - Pull top genes, filter to a gene family, check the biology - Look up any gene across **every sample your lab has sequenced** - Build an **IGV genome browser** view linked to the results ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} **Single-cell RNA-seq** - Browse the single-cell datasets the BRC hosts (76 today) - QC per sample or donor, cells per cluster - UMAPs, dot plots and violin plots - Marker genes between clusters or conditions **Everything** - Answers backed by **BRC training material**, with links - One shareable **report** at the end ::: :::: ## Example reports {.smaller} Each one was made in a single Claude session with the BRC plugin. :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} [![](../imgs/brc_bulk_volcano.png){fig-alt="Volcano plot of 4,639 genes changed between EpSC and SB samples." height="320px"}](../../data/brc_reports/BRC_bulk_RNAseq_report.html){target="_blank"} [**Bulk RNA-seq**](../../data/brc_reports/BRC_bulk_RNAseq_report.html){target="_blank"}: QC of 12 libraries (2 flagged), differential expression, and expression across 243 lab samples. ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} [![](../imgs/brc_sc_umap.png){fig-alt="UMAP of 15,457 human skin cells coloured by cluster." height="320px"}](../../data/brc_reports/BRC_scRNAseq_skin_report.html){target="_blank"} [**Single-cell RNA-seq**](../../data/brc_reports/BRC_scRNAseq_skin_report.html){target="_blank"}: young vs aged human skin (public data): QC per donor, clusters, cell types and composition. ::: :::: ::::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"} ::: notes Bulk data are real BRC pipeline data, anonymised for teaching (lab, user and sample names removed). The single-cell data are public: GSE130973, Solé-Boldo et al. 2020. Points to make: QC caught two weak libraries from the same animal; keratins confirm the groups; the SB "signal" is largely immune/melanocyte cells, i.e. composition. In single-cell, T cells are 17-22% of young-donor cells vs 1-3% old, and one cluster is a single-donor artefact. Both reports end with "check before you use": the AI ran BRC pipelines, the science is still yours. ::: ::::: ## Built for responsible use - **Your data stay on BRC servers.** Claude sees only the summaries and plots it asks for. - **Access follows your login**, scoped to your lab. - **Nothing expensive happens without you.** Anything that uses HPC compute shows a preview and waits for your OK. - **No invented numbers.** The plugin is told to copy every value from a BRC result, never from memory. - **The science is still yours.** Statistical and biological judgement goes to you and BRC staff, not the AI. Want to try it, or need an analysis reviewed? **brc@rockefeller.edu** ## Course and teaching materials ??Link to BRC training materials and how they can be used with AI tools (e.g. as context to supply in a prompt).?? ## Skills, templates and shared configuration ??Examples of packaged instructions, project templates or configuration files the BRC provides so that everyone starts from the same good defaults. Links to the *Customizing Your LLM* and *AI in Your Workflow* sections.?? # Working with the BRC {#working-with-the-brc background-color="#23373B" .center .middle} ## When to talk to us ??When to contact the BRC: reviewing an AI-assisted analysis, choosing a method, setting up a reproducible workflow, a new tool you want to try.?? ## Feedback and community contributions ??How to send feedback, request tools and contribute (the AI Strategy section says community contributions are welcome).?? ## Contact ??Contact details and where to find BRC resources.??
